speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information given the declining traditional letter mail volumes, what measures are being taken to ensure that Singapore Post’s domestic post and parcel business remains viable and there is continuity of postal services for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: As a public postal licencee, SingPost bears primary responsibility for providing Singapore's postal service and is allowed to access and operate postal infrastructure, such as the national postal code system and physical letterboxes to support this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: At the same time, SingPost is constituted as a commercial entity with obligations to its shareholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: As such, it must be able to maintain a viable business model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Many individuals have gone online, opting for paperless communications for convenience and cost savings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: At the same time, most Government agencies have digitalised, communicating with citizens through online channels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Today, businesses account for more than 80% of mail users and the average consumer sends less than one letter per month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: With this decline, it will be challenging for SingPost to continue running a viable business with its current operating model and at the current postage rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: As such, a balance must be struck to allow SingPost to fulfil its responsibilities in a sustainable manner, while ensuring the continuity of postal services for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: IMDA will also review the current postal service obligations to ensure that they remain relevant in today's highly digitalised context, especially given the many alternative electronic communication channels available to consumers and businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Domestic postal rates have largely been held constant since 2014, apart from a small increase at the start of the year.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Given the decline in volume and given that I can understand SingPost having their challenges, how does the Ministry ensure that there is no degradation of services that are provided by SingPost?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Could the Senior Minister of State give an indication of the quantum we are looking at, in terms of the adjustment?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As we go about doing this restructuring, I hope we pay a lot of attention to making sure that the jobs are preserved and we do all our best to keep as many of them in their current employment or in new jobs.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: IMDA, as the postal regulator, will continue to ensure that the postal licensee keeps up and complies with the quality of service.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These factors will be considered as part of the discussions.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Thirdly, on the part about local employees, this something that we are mindful of.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I am sure that SingPost, as a responsible employer, would be mindful of this as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In fact, I think there are regular conversations between them and the unions representing the postal employees.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, these are the issues that we have to discuss as part of the overall discussion around the future of the postal services, and as part of the discussions between the regulator and the licensee.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Just one supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: He referred to the service quality framework that the Government uses vis-à-vis SingPost because SingPost is a Government licencee.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Are there periodic surveys of customer satisfaction similar to what is done by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) vis-à-vis the public transport system, for example?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I am not suggesting that that be done necessarily every year.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: But is that something that is done regularly and is that something where the Government will discuss the findings and hold SingPost accountable?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Before I end, I just declare my interest as chairman of a company that does market research and consulting.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I would invite him to file a Parliamentary Question and we can take a look at that.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But broadly, let me set the context by saying that the quality of service framework, which broadly looks at the service level agreement between the licensee and its customers, and how it delivers the basic postal mails, these are issues that have been around for many, many years.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is something that was continually refined to make sure that it meets the needs of the consumers in Singapore and the needs of the licensees.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are things that we benchmark with the rest of the world.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In fact, Singapore has one of the most stringent quality of service framework compared to comparable cities and countries around the world.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Do these discussions involve the direct subsidising or funding of the company in relation to this aspect?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: First, about the recourse that the Government, as a regulator, has in respect of the terms and conditions of the licence.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is actually operating a business in Singapore and has applied for a licence to do so.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I hope that helps to address Mr Chua's first question around the obligations and recourse.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are all part and parcel of the terms and conditions of the licence and its regulated operations.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The second question is around the commercial aspect.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Like I mentioned earlier, SingPost is a publicly listed company and has its own set of corporate governance rules around its financial statements and its own set of considerations that it shares with its shareholders.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And when it talked about its specific segment of post and parcels, we should see that in that context as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Lastly, can the Member Mr Chua repeat the second question or have I answered all the questions?
